title: Inner product against a polynomial
statement: For any natural number $n$, any real coefficient family $p$ indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and any real-valued function $u$ on the Boolean cube, the uniform inner product of the polynomial represented by $p$ with $u$ equals $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\widehat u(S)$, where $\widehat u(S)$ is the Fourier--Walsh coefficient of $u$ at $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of the coordinate set
$u$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. For every real cube function $u$, $\mathbb E[Pu]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\widehat u(S)$.
